title: Cybersecurity Tops the Asia-Pacific Board Agenda for 2027, While Only 15% of Leaders are Very Confident in Risk Oversight
headline: Diligent report finds 29% of APAC boards see AI adoption outpacing governance
summary: A report by Diligent Institute shows that 29% of surveyed Asia-Pacific governance leaders believe AI adoption is outpacing governance within their organisations. Only 15% of respondents felt very confident in their board's ability to oversee significant risks, citing insufficient time and lack of relevant expertise. Furthermore, 62% of respondents identified digital technology, including AI and data management, as their primary board skills gap.
why_it_matters: The findings highlight a critical gap in board-level technical fluency and risk oversight across the region as organisations accelerate AI deployment ahead of formal governance controls.

quotes.text: 29% of respondents say AI adoption is ahead of governance.
Digital technology, including AI and data management, is the most frequently cited board skills gap (62%), more than twice as often as cybersecurity (29%), the second-most cited option.

classification.significance_reason: Provides empirical survey data on board-level AI governance gaps, skills shortages, and unapproved AI tool usage across the APAC region.
